calls.head: Stay out of the box, Canucks
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is the worst. The Canucks need to stay out of the box. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

calls.body: On depth, Vancouver is one of the league’s best, but Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Canucks.

surprises.head: Vancouver couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Vancouver’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Draisaitl has two goals and an assist as the Oilers get past the Canucks
paras: Mattias Ekholm struck first for the Oilers midway through the first, but Max Sasson tied it up for Vancouver with just nine seconds left in the period. The Oilers’ Ryan Nugent-Hopkins left early in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a head injury. The third period was a wild one. Jason Dickinson and Leon Draisaitl scored a little over three minutes apart early in the period to put the Oilers up 3-1. With the goalie pulled and two and a half minutes left, Brock Boeser cut Edmonton’s lead to 3-2, with Filip Hronek picking up his 300th NHL point on the goal. Draisaitl scored again into the empty net with 45 seconds left. Zach Hyman was back in the lineup after missing five games, and picked up an assist. Two players had three-point nights: Connor McDavid with three assists, and Draisaitl with two goals and an assist.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Devon Levi made 20 saves for the Oilers, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 26 of 29 at the other end. The Oilers moved to 12-3-3, still first in the Pacific, while the Canucks dropped to 3-15-1, still last in the NHL.
